question: Can a nonlinear scalar concept encoded by an internal neuron be recovered as a human-readable equation without knowing candidate concepts in advance?

key_findings.claim: The method defines two scalar functions as encoding the same local concept when their gradients are parallel on the data manifold, thereby making the interpretation invariant to an unknown invertible scalar reparameterization of the latent neuron.
key_findings.evidence: Section 3 constructs an equivalence class around the target neuron and uses normalized input-gradient alignment as its computable membership criterion rather than matching activation values directly.

anchors.section: Section 3.2, equivalence class of concept encodings

key_findings.claim: A genetic symbolic search minimizes mean squared error between normalized gradients of a candidate expression and the chosen neuron, then uses a complexity-loss Pareto front to select a closed form.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithms 2 and 3 compute input gradients, normalize them, evolve symbolic trees under a user-supplied operator set, and rank expressions by fit and complexity.

key_findings.claim: Across 12 synthetic Siamese-network tasks, the approach recovers the intended matrix invariant or dynamical conserved quantity in every case, with one reported approximation corrected after increasing the dataset to 200,000 examples.
key_findings.evidence: Tables 1-3 list trace, determinant, principal-minor, Lorentz, energy, and momentum expressions. The discussion says experiment 8 initially recovers a fourth-order approximation and finds the intended expression after expanding the sample.

key_findings.claim: Direct symbolic regression on the scalar latent activation succeeds on only 7 of 12 tasks in the authors' comparison because it must fit the network's nonlinear reparameterization as well as the concept.
key_findings.evidence: Section 4.2 and Appendix E compare activation-value regression with gradient-direction matching; the direct method primarily succeeds on traces and second-order polynomials and fails on more distorted latents.

key_findings.claim: The paper's general claim is narrower than arbitrary latent-space interpretation: the formalism treats a single differentiable scalar neuron whose concept has an expressible scalar equation and whose relevant input-gradient directions are nondegenerate on the sampled manifold.
key_findings.evidence: The conclusion explicitly limits the method by symbolic-search expressibility and the need to isolate concepts through a bottleneck or disentanglement; multi-neuron distributed concepts and zero gradients are not resolved by the experiments.

method.core_idea: Search for the simplest symbolic function with the same input-space level sets as a selected latent neuron, avoiding the need to reproduce the neuron's arbitrary nonlinear scale.
method.mechanism: Train a bottlenecked Siamese network on transformation-related triplets, sample input gradients of one latent coordinate, normalize those gradients, evolve symbolic expressions, and minimize directional gradient mismatch plus expression complexity.
assumptions: One neuron isolates the scientific concept as a differentiable scalar function.
Parallel gradients on the sampled data manifold identify the desired equivalence class.
The intended concept lies in the supplied symbolic operator grammar.
Sampling covers regions needed to distinguish a global law from a local approximation.

techniques.role: Matches level-set geometry while ignoring monotone latent reparameterization.
Learns a latent invariant from transformation-related examples.
Balances gradient fit against symbolic complexity.

evaluations.setting: 12 synthetic matrix-invariant, Lorentz-invariant, and conserved-dynamics datasets with 50K training triplets, 5K validation triplets, and 10K test triplets each
evaluations.metric: Qualitative equality or approximation of the retrieved closed form
evaluations.result: The intended equation or a close equivalent is reported for all 12 tasks; one local approximation requires a 200K-sample rerun to recover the intended global form.
evaluations.baseline: Known ground-truth invariant or conserved quantity

evaluations.result: Direct symbolic regression on latent values succeeds on 7 of 12 tasks versus all 12 for normalized-gradient search in the reported comparison.
evaluations.baseline: Direct PySR-style regression of latent activation values

limitations: The method interprets one scalar neuron at a time and assumes concept isolation or disentanglement.
Recovery is limited to the selected symbolic grammar and genetic-search budget.
All demonstrations use synthetic tasks with known ground truth and deliberately generated symmetries.
Normalized gradients are unstable at stationary points and can be sensitive to noisy derivatives.
A local approximation can look correct when the sampled domain is too narrow.
failure_modes: A concept distributed across several neurons has no faithful single-coordinate equation.
Two different global functions can have nearly parallel gradients on a sparsely sampled manifold.
A missing primitive in the symbolic grammar prevents recovery regardless of latent quality.
Finite-difference or backpropagation noise can distort direction after normalization near zero norm.
reusable_insights: Interpret level-set geometry instead of activation magnitude when a latent coordinate may be nonlinearly reparameterized.
Stress-test symbolic discoveries by expanding the sampled domain and checking intervention-invariant predictions.
Separate latent-concept discovery, concept isolation, and equation search as independently testable modules.
open_questions: How can the equivalence-class criterion be extended from one scalar neuron to distributed vector-valued concepts?
Can uncertainty over symbolic expressions distinguish global laws from locally indistinguishable approximations?
Does the method recover unknown equations from noisy real experiments without ground-truth transformations?

competitive_landscape.title: Discovering Symbolic Models from Deep Learning with Inductive Biases
competitive_landscape.relationship: Symbolic extraction from learned scientific models
competitive_landscape.difference: Cranmer et al. apply symbolic regression to modular learned relations; symbolic gradients instead target arbitrary nonlinear scalar latent encodings through level-set direction rather than output-value fidelity.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretability Beyond Feature Attribution: Quantitative Testing with Concept Activation Vectors
competitive_landscape.difference: TCAV tests sensitivity to a user-defined concept direction; this work searches without a supplied concept label and returns a closed-form scalar equation.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpreting Deep Visual Representations via Network Dissection
competitive_landscape.difference: Network Dissection aligns units with a predefined visual concept vocabulary; symbolic gradients target quantitative scientific concepts and generate equations from an operator grammar.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Symbolic Regression: Recovering Mathematical Expressions from Data via Risk-Seeking Policy Gradients
competitive_landscape.difference: Deep Symbolic Regression fits observed target values directly; the reviewed method changes the objective to normalized gradients of an internal neuron to quotient out unknown scalar distortion.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Normalized symbolic gradients provide the first general route to closed-form interpretation of nonlinearly distorted single-neuron latent scientific concepts without prior candidate knowledge.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The equivalence-class construction motivates an implementable objective and outperforms direct latent-value symbolic regression on 12 controlled tasks.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Quotienting out scalar reparameterization is a strong and reusable idea, but 'general' should be read as scalar, differentiable, symbolically expressible, and sufficiently sampled rather than arbitrary latent interpretation.

reviewer_notes: Read all 26 extracted pages, including the equivalence construction, algorithms, 12 task tables, approximation audit, direct-regression appendix, and limitations. Competing primary records were checked on arXiv on 2026-08-23.
